description.xml:
Register the specified Licenses in the System. Each License should be bound via Hardware Id to some Server in the System.
The License Block can be obtained via the procedure offered in the VMS Client application, menu System Administration -> Licenses -> Manual Activation.

The parameters should be passed as a JSON array of objects in POST message body with content type "application/json". An example of such array can be seen in the result of GET /ec2/getLicenses.
License serial number. Corresponds to the License Block SERIAL property.

License Block - a plain-text "property" file (with "key=value" lines). It is generated by the License Server, is bound to the particular Server (via Hardware Id), and is signed (the signature is stored in one of the properties). The License Block contains the following properties (keys):
  • NAME VMS product name.
  • SERIAL Serial number of the License.
  • HWID Hardware Id of the Server to which the License is bound.
  • COUNT Number of cameras which are covered by the License.
  • CLASS Type of the License. Defines which VMS platforms can use the License, and for what kind of camera-like devices.
  • VERSION VMS version.
  • BRAND VMS product name.
  • EXPIRATION Expiration date in format YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS. Optional; if omitted, the License lifetime is unlimited.
  • SIGNATURE2 Digital signature created by the License Server.
  • COMPANY VMS vendor.
Additionally, other proprietary keys may appear in the License Block.

description.xml:
The Server may process requests by HTTP and RTSP protocols as well as HTTPS and RTSPS protocols (HTTP and RTSP over encrypted connection).
  • Protocols supported by default: TLS 1.1 and TLS 1.2.
  • Deprecated protocols (disabled by default): SSL 3 and TLS 1.0.

This method is preferable for external applications, most of HTTP libraries support it.
Server is fully conformant with the authentication defined in rfc2617 (https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc2617).

This method should only be used in browser javascript applications which share the origin with the Server (e.g. application and the Server are accessible by the a single gateway).
Cookie authorization scheme allows to avoid standard login/password dialog in web-applications.
It provides you a way to replace it with your own dialog.
It works mostly like sessions, but is a bit more secure because it doesn't send user's password over HTTP.
  • To check authentication:
    1. Call GET /api/getCurrentUser
    2. You will get 401 (Unauthorised) in case you need authorization
    3. You will get 200 (OK) and the user object otherwise
  • To log in:
    1. Call GET /api/getNonce
    2. In response you'll get a JSON object with realm and nonce (nonce is a session key for this user)
    3. Calculate authentication hash auth_digest, using realm and nonce (see algorithm below)
    4. Call POST /api/cookieLogin and pass the "auth" parameter in the json request body
    5. Server will check authentication and set session cookies
  • Executing requests:
    1. Session cookie should be supplied with every request, browser does it automatically if cookies are enabled
    2. HTTP header X-Runtime-Guid should contain the key from x-runtime-guid cookie value
  • To log out:
    1. Call POST /api/cookieLogout
    2. Server will clear the session cookies

This method should only be used if other methods are not applicable, e.g. webm direct link or javascript application with different origin.
Add the "auth" parameter to the URL query section of any HTTP request:
  • Call /api/getNonce to get realm and nonce from the server (the current server time is used as a nonce value, and the nonce is valid for about 5 minutes)
  • Calculate the authentication hash auth_digest, using realm and nonce (see algorithm below)
  • Specify the authentication hash in the URL parameter: http://127.0.0.1:7001/method?auth=auth_digest&other_params

For URL-based authentication and cookie-based authentication you need to calculate the hash manually, using the following algorithm:
  • Call GET /api/getNonce
  • In response you'll get a JSON object with realm and nonce
  • Translate user's username to the lower case
  • Check the required method ("GET" for HTTP GET requests, "POST" for HTTP POST requests, "PLAY" for RTSP etc)
  • digest = md5_hex(user_name + ":" + realm + ":" + password)
  • partial_ha2 = md5_hex(method + ":")
  • simplified_ha2 = md5_hex(digest + ":" + nonce + ":" + partial_ha2)
  • auth_digest = base64(user_name + ":" + nonce + ":" + simplified_ha2)
  • Here auth_digest is the required authentication hash
